title: Decoupling 2D translation-invariant topological CSS codes
authors: Yifei Wang, Zhongyi Ni, Mingxin He, Jinguo Liu, Yingfei Gu
abstract: Two-dimensional translation-invariant topological CSS codes on qubits are known to be locally equivalent, after coarse-graining, to stacks of toric codes. However, existing constructions generally break more translation symmetry than is required to remove anyon-permuting translations, leaving open whether any further obstruction exists. We prove that no such obstruction occurs: after passing to the maximal anyon-preserving superlattice, every such code admits a local unitary decoupling into toric codes and product states. We further provide an efficient algorithm for explicitly constructing the decoupling map, together with bounds on the required supercell size and operator spreading. The decoupling requires no additional ancillas in generic cases and extends to finite systems with suitable boundary conditions.
summary: This paper mathematically proves that 2D translation-invariant topological CSS codes can always be locally unitarily decoupled into a combination of toric codes and product states. The authors provide an efficient algorithm based on module theory over Laurent polynomials to construct this decoupling map, simplifying the understanding and implementation of these quantum error-correcting codes.
main_problem: To prove that no further obstruction exists beyond removing anyon-permuting translations when decoupling 2D translation-invariant topological CSS codes into toric codes and product states.
main_result: The authors prove this non-existence of obstruction, showing every such code admits a local unitary decoupling into toric codes and product states after passing to the maximal anyon-preserving superlattice.
method: The core method involves applying module theory over Laurent polynomials ($R = \mathbb{F}_2[x\pm 1, y\pm 1]$) and advanced linear algebra techniques to find required chain isomorphisms between complex structures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional (2D) translation-invariant topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes defined by Pauli Hamiltonians. These are analyzed using module theory over the Laurent polynomial ring, relating them to toric codes and product states.
key_observables: Logical error rate, support spreading $s(Q)$, number of e-anyons ($t$), and the existence/invertibility of chain isomorphisms.
important_parameters: The density of qubits per unit cell ($q$) and the dimensions related to stabilizer generators ($r$ and $s$).
main_assumptions: Previous constructions break more symmetry than necessary; the analysis relies on module theory over non-field rings, which complicates standard linear algebra techniques.
figures_summary: One figure summary mentions a speed-accuracy tradeoff comparison between decoding methods (unitary-decouple vs. BP-OSD), and another table quantifies support spreading for transported CNOTs.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical framework using module theory over Laurent polynomials, proves the existence of the decoupling map via chain isomorphism construction, provides an efficient algorithm to compute this map, and discusses applications like gate construction and decoding performance.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (module theory) to simplify complex quantum error-correcting codes into known, simpler structures (toric codes), which is fundamental for building scalable quantum computation architectures.
